text:
riley: hit a funky case in staging: upstream worker OOMs mid-stream and client gets a few tokens then nothing. no trailer, UI spins. we need a concrete contract for graceful eviction and clear client signals.

omar: saw same. current behavior is connection RST -> client treats as terminal. we need a recoverable indicator so clients can surface partial+retry.

tess: two angles: signaling (trailers vs inline control frames) and state (stateless token vs server-side resume). both have ops/billing tradeoffs.

lee: proposal: unify as a "control frame" contract. on graceful eviction the gateway emits either an HTTP trailer or a small JSON control chunk inline: `{\"_rw_evict\":{...}}`. fields: evict_id, offset, checksum, resume_available, reason. clients parse either form.

riley: example inline chunk we used in tests: {"_rw_evict":{"evict_id":"9f8a..","offset":3072,"checksum":"a3b2","reason":"mem_pressure","resume_available":true,"ttl":60}}

omar: for transports without trailers (HTTP/1 fetch) inline chunk covers it. for HTTP/2+ prefer trailers: x-rw-evict-id, x-rw-offset, x-rw-checksum, x-rw-resume-available, grpc-status:8

tess: resume modes: stateless vs stateful. stateless = signed resume-token that contains offset+variant+ttl; no server state. cheap but may replay more tokens on resume. stateful = gateway stores small resume objects TTLed for quick resume with KV cache. heavier memory needs but faster resume.

lee: route config: `resume_policy: stateless|stateful|disabled`, checkpoint_interval: 128, resume_ttl_seconds: 45, admission_mbs: "tenant-scoped". default stateless.

riley: billing rules: initial tokens billed normally. resumed tokens billed to the retrying request. server-side replay to rehydrate state (stateful) counted as compute-overhead metric and billed separately. track metrics: edge.evict.issued, edge.evict.resumed, edge.evict.fallback, edge.resume.replay_ms.

omar: admission control: stateful resume uses mb-seconds accounting per tenant. if quota exhausted gateway still emits control frame but sets resume_available=false and adds x-rw-resume-fallback:true on fallback response.

tess: client UX: if resume_available -> show partial + "Retry and continue". retry flow: client sends header x-rw-resume: <evict_id|token>. gateway validates and either routes to resume entry or model-short variant. if resume missing, gateway attaches x-rw-resume-fallback:true.

lee: security: tokens must not include PII. stateless token = signed payload with route+offset+v+ttl and short fingerprint only. key-rotation plan required. evict_id must be unguessable.

riley: tests: chaos harness inject soft/hard evicts at random offsets; assert client sees control frame or trailer; assert resume flow recovers continuity within allowed drift. add fuzz tests across HTTP/1/2/3.

omar: ops runbook snippet: alert if EVICT_FALLBACK_RATE > 5% for 10m. if high: check resume-store memory, tenant mb-second usage, checkpoint frequency.

tess: SDK teams: expose ResumeManager parseControl(rawChunk|trailers) -> {resumeMeta} and a resume API to call. ship Node/Python helpers to keep client parsing consistent.

edge-bot: canary deploy queued: gateway/edge-proxy v1.48.0 -> us-west-2 :rocket:

lee: i'll write RFC with contract (control frame + trailer schemas), route knobs, admission & billing, SDK contract, test plan, and rollout strategy. link when ready.

riley: adding small note: prefer stateless default for scale but allow stateful opt-in for enterprise customers who require exact byte-for-byte resume.

edge-bot: deploy succeeded: gateway/edge-proxy v1.48.0 canary -> 2/3 hosts (us-west-2) succeeded.
